headline: Consensus workflows merge evidence for eukaryotic genome and sequence annotation
label: Genome Annotation Pipelines
summary: Recent published pipelines integrate multiple evidence sources to scale annotation and alignment of large eukaryotic and DNA sequence datasets.
synthesis: The dominant thread is algorithmic reuse and evidence integration for scalable sequence analysis. OMAnnotator repurposes the OMA orthology algorithm to merge ab initio, transcriptomic and homology gene predictions into a single consensus eukaryotic genome annotation, using orthology inference as the mechanism for combining sources. deMEM addresses scale at the alignment step: a divide-and-conquer framework built on de Bruijn graph maximum exact matches allows MAFFT to handle very large DNA multiple sequence alignments. nf-core/proteinfamilies packages protein family generation and assignment of new sequences to existing families as an open-source Nextflow pipeline. What is new in this set is the use of orthology inference to produce consensus gene models, while the other two items emphasize scalability of alignment and family assignment rather than genome annotation itself.
